record.paper_title: Open problems in dynamics and related fields
record.original_question: Can one find a triangle whose angles are Diophantine modulo 2π and whose billiard flow is ergodic with respect to Liouville measure?

evidence.quote: QUESTION 30 (A. Katok). Find a triangle whose angles are Diophantine (mod 2π) with ergodic (with respect to the Liouville measure) billia rd ﬂow.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a triangle $T \subset \mathbb{R}^2$ with interior angles $\alpha_1, \alpha_2, \alpha_3$ (satisfying $\alpha_1+\alpha_2+\alpha_3=\pi$). The billiard flow on $T$ is the geodesic flow on the unit tangent bundle of $T$, where a point particle moves in straight lines inside $T$ and reflects elastically (angle of incidence equals angle of reflection) at the boundary. This flow preserves the Liouville measure (the product of Lebesgue measure on $T$ with the uniform measure on the unit circle of directions).

Call a real number $\theta$ Diophantine modulo $2\pi$ if there exist constants $C>0$ and $\tau \geq 0$ such that for every nonzero integer $q$ and every integer $p$,
$$\left| \frac{\theta}{2\pi} - \frac{p}{q} \right| \geq \frac{C}{|q|^{2+\tau}}.$$

Question: Does there exist a triangle whose three angles $\alpha_1, \alpha_2, \alpha_3$ are all Diophantine modulo $2\pi$ and whose billiard flow is ergodic with respect to the Liouville measure?
artifact.status_search_result: Ergodicity of polygonal billiards with Diophantine angles is regarded as one of the central open problems in the dynamics of polygonal billiards. While ergodicity is known to hold for a residual (dense $G_\delta$) set of polygons (Kerckhoff–Masur–Smillie, Zemlyakov–Katok), no explicit triangle—let alone one with Diophantine angles—has been shown to be ergodic, and no general approach is known. The problem appears still open as of recent surveys.

status_evidence.title: Open problems in elliptic dynamics (A. Katok)
status_evidence.snippet: It is assumed that for typical Diophantine values of the vector of angles the billiard is ergodic, but up to now no serious approaches to this problem are known.
status_evidence.claim: Katok states the problem is open with no known approach.

status_evidence.title: Survey lecture on billiards (R. E. Schwartz)
status_evidence.snippet: The set of ergodic n-gons is residual ... open problem is whether the measure of ergodic n-gons is positive.
status_evidence.claim: Ergodicity for typical/Diophantine polygons remains open.
